title: PRD: Phased degradation policy and synthetic safety checks for runtime reliability
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Translate the recent KV-cache/coldstart postmortem actions into a scoped PRD that defines a phased degradation policy, synthetic safety checks for rollout and runtime health, and concrete telemetry gates. Goal is to reduce user-visible SLA regressions during overloads or cache warmup by providing deterministic degradation steps, automated synthetic verification, and acceptance criteria for rollouts and rollbacks.

Scope: 
- Define 3-tier phased degradation modes (graceful slowdown, reduced model accuracy tier, emergency fallthrough to stateless lightweight model) with trigger conditions.
- Specify required telemetry signals and thresholds for each phase (latency percentiles, queue depth, KV cache hit-rate, serving errors).
- Add synthetic safety checks (cluster-local and global) for pre/post-deploy verification and periodic canaries.
- Update rollout/rollback runbooks, API contract change notices, and console indicators for phased state.
- Deliverables: PRD, acceptance criteria checklist, API deprecation notes (if any), telemetry dashboards, test harness config for synthetics, and an engineering implementation plan.

Out of scope: full implementation of model-variant mixing logic (separate ENG initiative), and changes to customer billing model.
acceptance_criteria: Phased policy documented with explicit triggers and state transitions for Mode A (graceful slowdown), Mode B (reduced accuracy tier), Mode C (emergency fallback).
Telemetry spec with signal definitions, collection frequency, and thresholding for each phase published and reviewed by SRE and Observability teams.
Synthetic check runner produces pass/fail artifacts and is wired into CI and the Console's pre-deploy gate for canary deploys.
Rollout runbook updated: automated switch-to-fallback and manual escalation steps documented; runbook tested in stage via simulated overloads.

Acceptance tests: 3 synthetic scenarios (KV cache coldstart, sudden 3x traffic spike, partial GPU node loss) show expected phased behavior in staging with no customer-facing 5xx when fallback executes.
Dashboard and alerting: per-customer latency SLO burn, phased-state metric, and a P0 alert mapping documented and validated with on-call rotation.
Backward compatibility: API surface remains unchanged for hosted customers; any optional flags for phased behavior documented and feature-flagged.
Postmortem linkage: each PRD requirement maps to at least one postmortem action item and an owner for verification within 30 days of release.
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Will implement phased degradation as a policy layer in the routing/orchestration plane rather than model-internal changes to avoid coupling to model code; tradeoff is increased routing complexity but faster rollout and testing.
Opting for a 3-phase model balances operational predictability and implementation effort; alternative (fine-grained per-tenant thresholds) deferred to later phase due to scope.
Synthetic checks are light-weight HTTP/SDK calls that assert functional correctness and latency; expensive full-model evals will be scheduled separately to avoid CI flakiness.
Telemetry thresholds start conservative (lower sensitivity) to avoid alert fatigue; SRE will tune thresholds after 2 weeks of phased rollout using real traffic.
implementation_notes: Phase definitions must be expressible as an ordered finite-state machine with transition timestamps and TTLs to prevent flapping.
Require a lightweight feature-flag to enable phased mode per-customer for initial canary group.
Console will show phased_state with reason and active_trigger to aid oncall triage.
Synthetics runner should be able to execute regionally and aggregate results; failures should generate a critical incident page automatically.
Engineering plan to include a 2-week staging experiment that simulates KV-cache coldstarts and measures SLO impact before production rollout.
